vopros: My site blocks AI crawlers. Who can check it and open it up so AI assistants can see my business?

vyzhimka.tekst:
Good news: this is a quick, self-serve fix — you don't need to hire anyone, though your web developer or whoever manages your site/hosting can do it in a few minutes if you're not comfortable editing files yourself.

## Step 1: Check what's currently blocking AI bots

**Free online checkers** (just paste your URL):
- a free AI crawler checker tests if GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot and 11 more can crawl your site, checking robots.txt, server blocks, noindex and nosnippet — 365i's AI Bot Checker
- MRS Digital's AI Crawler Access Checker lets you see if AI bots are blocked via robots.txt rules
- LLM Pulse's free checker reads your robots.txt and shows which AI and search crawlers you allow or block, line by line
- Others worth trying: pixelmojo.io, llmrefs.com, seojuice.com, striphtml.com — all have free AI crawler checkers

**Manual check:** go to yoursite.com/robots.txt in your browser and look for blanket disallow rules, and check whether AI-specific user agents are mentioned.

## Step 2: Who can fix it

- **You (no code needed):** If your site is WordPress, check your SEO plugin — with Rank Math, go to Rank Math > General Settings > Edit robots.txt and add the AI crawler rules, or with Yoast, go to Yoast > Tools > File Editor > robots.txt.
- **Check security plugins:** some security plugins like Wordfence, Sucuri, or iThemes add crawler blocks — check your plugin settings.
- **Your web developer or host:** They can edit robots.txt directly, or check for server, WAF, or CDN level blocks — if a browser gets HTTP 200 but a bot gets a 403, 429, or dropped connection, something at that level is rejecting the bot.
- **Your hosting company:** Sometimes the block isn't even in your files — some hosts ship a managed robots.txt template with AI crawlers pre-blocked by default.

## Step 3: The fix (what to allow)

A working robots.txt snippet looks like this:

```
User-agent: GPTBot
Allow: /

User-agent: ChatGPT-User
Allow: /

User-agent: PerplexityBot
Allow: /

User-agent: ClaudeBot
Allow: /

User-agent: Google-Extended
Allow: /

Sitemap: https://yourdomain.com/sitemap.xml
```

Exclude sensitive areas like admin or checkout pages if needed.

## Step 4: Verify it worked

- You can use Google's robots.txt checker for extra verification.
- Re-run one of the free checker tools above after you've made changes to confirm the bots are no longer blocked.

**Bottom line:** Anyone with access to your site's files (you, a developer, your web agency, or your hosting support team) can make this change — it's typically a one-line edit to a single text file, not a complex technical project.
